evals.prompt: I want to make $1 million by the end of the year, but the size of that goal makes me avoid working on it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the $1 million ambition as direction but removes it from this week's active focus; proposes one signed, paid $10,000 customer as the focused mission for the next seven days; gives one immediate move toward that customer; and avoids a full-year decomposition, formal planning card, or intake barrage.
assertions: Preserves the $1 million ambition without making it the active weekly workload
Makes one signed or paid $10,000 customer the focused seven-day mission
Concentrates attention on that one commercial result rather than decomposing the remaining revenue target
Ends with one immediate action that directly advances the customer mission
Uses natural, low-pressure language instead of a formal card or preliminary questionnaire

farplane.title: Intimidating revenue target becomes one focused customer mission
farplane.notes: Canonical regression derived from the operator-accepted behavior: preserve the ambition, collapse the active horizon, and pursue one meaningful paid result.

evals.prompt: I want to publish 30 videos before the end of the year. Every time I picture all 30, I freeze and publish nothing.
evals.expected_output: Leaves 30 videos as the direction while making one finished and published video the only active mission for the next seven days; narrows the video enough to ship; gives one immediate production move; and does not plan all 30 videos or reduce the mission to preparation only.
assertions: Keeps the larger publishing ambition visible but inactive for the current push
Chooses one actually published video as the meaningful near-term result
Does not create a calendar or production plan for all 30 videos
Avoids substituting research, equipment, branding, or outlining for publication
Gives one immediate move toward finishing the selected video

farplane.title: Video volume becomes one publication mission
farplane.notes: Held-out transfer case for horizon collapse without trivializing the outcome.

evals.prompt: I want 10,000 people using my app. I keep expanding the roadmap because the goal feels enormous, and I still haven't put it in anyone's hands.
evals.expected_output: Keeps 10,000 users as direction but makes one real person successfully using the smallest core workflow the focused near-term mission; rejects roadmap expansion as the active work; defines the result as observed use rather than setup; and gives one immediate move toward reaching that user.
assertions: Moves the 10,000-user ambition out of the active horizon without dismissing it
Chooses one real user's completed core workflow as the focused result
Rejects roadmap expansion or preparation as a substitute for user contact
Keeps the mission meaningful and end-to-end rather than a trivial micro-task
Provides one immediate action toward getting the product into that user's hands

farplane.title: Large adoption goal becomes one real-user mission
farplane.notes: Held-out case tests transfer from a commercial precedent to product adoption.

evals.prompt: I landed one $2,000 consulting client last month. I want a $100,000 business, but thinking about all the remaining clients makes me want to redesign everything.
evals.expected_output: Uses the completed client as evidence, keeps $100,000 as direction, and focuses the next seven days on winning one comparable paid client by reusing what already worked; avoids restarting with positioning or infrastructure; and ends with one direct sales action.
assertions: Treats the existing paid client as evidence rather than restarting from zero
Makes the next comparable paid client the active mission
Uses the existing sales path before recommending redesign or infrastructure
Does not calculate or plan the entire remaining $98,000
Ends with one immediate action toward the strongest plausible next buyer

farplane.title: Existing commercial proof becomes the next focused repetition
farplane.notes: Boundary case: an accepted precedent should advance from real evidence rather than repeat a first-proof ritual.

evals.prompt: I want to run a half marathon in two months, but the full training plan feels like a second job. This week I can train three times and I have no injury constraints.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the half marathon as direction and makes one completed three-session training week the focused mission; uses the supplied capacity instead of inventing more; avoids presenting the full two-month program; and gives one immediate action that starts the first session or commits its concrete start.
assertions: Preserves the half-marathon ambition while narrowing the active horizon to this week
Uses the supplied three-session capacity as the meaningful mission
Does not expand into a full training plan or invent additional capacity
Keeps the focused mission substantial rather than reducing it to preparation
Ends with one immediate move toward the first training session

farplane.title: Training-plan pressure becomes one honest training week
farplane.notes: Held-out personal-goal case tests capacity-respecting horizon collapse.
